bull_bear.body:
- Traveller maintained clear leadership in the core van segment, commanding over 70% market share
- Decade-plus contract manufacturing relationships with global OEMs: the 100,000th engine for BMW India was built during the year, and the 200,000th engine for Mercedes-Benz India followed, a relationship spanning over 50 years
- Debt-free position during the year, with the Board's Report noting zero debt service obligation and interest coverage improving sharply
- Joint venture with Rolls Royce Solutions GmbH (Force MTU Power Systems Private Limited, 51% held) gives access to global powertrain technology
- Engineering capability in purpose-built and defence vehicles, evidenced by the first lot of Gurkha vehicles supplied to the Indian Army
- Application-based, multi-driveline approach (efficient ICE, CNG and electric solutions) rather than a single-technology bet
- Broad-based platform growth in FY26: Urbania recorded over 100% volume growth and Trax over 70% growth, reducing dependence on a single platform
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Powertrain technology transition risk — no single winning technology — The MD&A states the industry is passing through a period of significant technological change with emphasis on electrification, alternative fuels and cleaner technologies, but that the transition will take place at different speeds across segments. The Company must fund parallel development of efficient ICE, CNG and electric drivelines without knowing which application shifts when; management explicitly says it will not assume one technology replaces all others.
- Geopolitical, energy and supply-chain disruption feeding into input costs — Management flags that recent geopolitical developments show how quickly events beyond India's borders can affect domestic industry, and that disruptions in energy and other essential inputs, rising commodity prices and disturbances to shipping and supply chains can impact both production and costs.
- Product quality, vehicle safety and customer-service failure (recall risk) — The BRSR materiality table identifies Customer Centricity as a risk: failure to meet changing customer expectations risks loss of loyalty and market share, while poor service can trigger legal action and negative publicity, and unattended vehicle safety issues can lead to accidents, injuries, fatalities and costly recalls.
- Occupational health and safety at manufacturing sites — The BRSR lists Occupational Health and Safety as a risk: failure to maintain a safe working environment and non-compliance with safety protocols by employees and business partners can cause casualties, significant legal liabilities and substantial fines, damage morale and productivity, and impair the ability to attract talent and secure affordable insurance.
- Regulatory, policy and tax change — The cautionary statement names changes in Government regulations, tax laws and other statutes among the important factors that could make actual results differ materially. The MD&A also argues that simplification of regulations, ease of establishing and expanding facilities and a stable policy environment are preconditions for industry to invest with confidence — i.e. the current environment is a constraint as much as a support.
- Demand cyclicality and price conditions in the served markets — The cautionary statement identifies economic conditions affecting demand/supply and price conditions in the markets in which the Company operates as a key swing factor. Force Motors' end-segments — tour and travel, school transport, employee commuting, hospitality, tourism, healthcare — are discretionary and cyclical, and FY26's growth was partly aided by one-off GST rate rationalisation improving affordability.
- Concentration on a few global OEM customers in the component business — The component business is described entirely in terms of two counterparties — engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India at Chakan and engines and CRFM modules for BMW India at Chennai. The stability the Board's Report attributes to this business is therefore dependent on a very small number of contractual relationships and their model cycles.
- Platform concentration — dependence on the Traveller franchise — The Board's Report attributes the year's performance to Traveller's clear leadership in the core van segment with over 70% market share, alongside newer platforms. A share that high in a single core segment is as much an exposure as a moat: it can only be defended, not grown, and any competitive or regulatory shift in that segment flows straight to group volumes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Force Motors designs and manufactures light commercial and passenger-carrier vehicles in India, spanning the Traveller van range, the premium Urbania platform, the Trax platform and purpose-built Special Vehicle Division products such as the Gurkha for institutional and defence customers. Alongside its own vehicle brands, the Company runs a contract component business, manufacturing engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India at a dedicated facility in Chakan, Pune, and engines and CRFM modules for BMW India at its Chennai facility. Its vehicles serve tour and travel, school transport, employee commuting and other specialised mobility applications, with growing emphasis on exports and on emerging drivelines including CNG and electric.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core vehicle businesses and reinforce leadership positions in chosen segments, pursuing growth with financial and operational discipline
- Application-based, multi-driveline product development — continued work on efficient ICE and CNG drivelines alongside electric mobility solutions, rather than assuming one technology replaces all others
- Refresh and premiumise the product portfolio: new-generation Traveller N range and Urbania DX, with Urbania positioned for premium passenger mobility
- Build out EV engineering capability, including an electric version of the Traveller platform and dedicated EV engineering infrastructure, assembly stations and a testing lab
- Expand geographically and place greater emphasis on exports, progressively preparing India-developed products for more sophisticated overseas markets
- Grow the defence and specialised mobility franchise through the Special Vehicle Division, building on purpose-built vehicle engineering (Gurkha supply to the Indian Army)
- Sustain the component contract-manufacturing business with global OEMs (engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India, engines and CRFM modules for BMW India)
- Keep R&D spend at a consistent percentage of revenue, anchored on the state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre in Pune driving new product development
- Increase the share of renewable energy in manufacturing as part of a responsible and sustainable manufacturing approach
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes expansion mainly in qualitative terms rather than as a capex programme. On the energy side, the Company commissioned a rooftop solar power plant at Pithampur during the year, increasing the share of green energy in its energy mix, and continues to target 50% green energy by 2027 with a longer-term Net Zero emissions goal by 2050. Product-side expansion came through the introduction of the new-generation Traveller N range and Urbania DX, and through the Special Vehicle Division supplying the first lot of Gurkha vehicles to the Indian Army, with management pointing to continued opportunities in defence and specialised mobility. Development capability is centred on the Company's state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre in Pune, which drives new product development, engineering and technology solutions. Inorganically, after the close of the financial year the Company acquired 100% of Veera Tanneries Private Limited (VTPL) for `16,196 lacs, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary, and approved a loan of up to `2,000 lacs to vendor PKN Motors Private Limited. Management also frames geographic expansion — pursuing a wider range of geographical markets and greater emphasis on exports — as the next leg of growth, supported by continued investment in technology, people, processes and market development. No plant-wise capacity addition, commissioning timeline or rupee capex quantum is stated in the routed sections; the two named capex disclosures supplied (capital commitments and segment capital expenditure) arrive as labels only, with no figures attached.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian commercial vehicle sales grew 12.6% to 10,79,871 units in FY 2025-26, crossing the one-million mark for the first time
- GST rate rationalisation during the year improved affordability and provided an impetus to demand across several vehicle categories
- India's passenger carrier market is expected to grow at an annual rate of 8-9% YOY for the next few years, with GDP growth expected around 7% YOY
- End-segments served by the Company — education, hospitality, tourism and healthcare — are expected to grow 1.5 to 2 times over the next five years, boosting demand for Force Motors' vehicles
- Demographic dividend and highway infrastructure investment expected to support passenger-carrier growth, with significant expansion in the last-mile connectivity segment the Company serves
- Growth of Global Capability Centres in India is raising demand for premium mobility, where the Company is positioned with Urbania
- EV penetration in medium-to-heavy passenger carriers is still early at 2-3%, leaving substantial headroom supported by government-led EV initiatives
- Healthy demand during the year across Tour and Travel, School Buses and buses for commuting professionals
- Broad-based platform performance: Traveller holding over 70% share of the core van segment, Urbania over 100% volume growth, Trax over 70% growth
- Electrification is expected to advance at different speeds across segments — electric mobility is most relevant for defined routes, higher daily mileage and last-mile applications, while conventional and alternative-fuel drivelines remain relevant elsewhere
- India's deeper trade engagement with major economies including the European Union creates a more favourable environment for Indian manufacturers with established global partnerships to expand internationally
- Watch item: geopolitical developments, energy and input availability, rising commodity prices and shipping/supply-chain disruption can impact both production and costs

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Force Motors is an Indian automotive manufacturer whose Traveller van platform commands over 70% market share in its core van segment, alongside a long-standing component business building engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India and BMW India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Force Motors designs and manufactures light commercial and passenger-carrier vehicles in India, spanning the Traveller van range, the premium Urbania platform, the Trax platform and purpose-built Special Vehicle Division products such as the Gurkha for institutional and defence customers. Alongside its own vehicle brands, the Company runs a contract component business, manufacturing engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India at a dedicated facility in Chakan, Pune, and engines and CRFM modules for BMW India at its Chennai facility. Its vehicles serve tour and travel, school transport, employee commuting and other specialised mobility applications, with growing emphasis on exports and on emerging drivelines including CNG and electric.

end_markets.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian commercial vehicle sales grew 12.6% to 10,79,871 units in FY 2025-26, crossing the one-million mark for the first time
- GST rate rationalisation during the year improved affordability and provided an impetus to demand across several vehicle categories
- India's passenger carrier market is expected to grow at an annual rate of 8-9% YOY for the next few years, with GDP growth expected around 7% YOY
- End-segments served by the Company — education, hospitality, tourism and healthcare — are expected to grow 1.5 to 2 times over the next five years, boosting demand for Force Motors' vehicles
- Demographic dividend and highway infrastructure investment expected to support passenger-carrier growth, with significant expansion in the last-mile connectivity segment the Company serves
- Growth of Global Capability Centres in India is raising demand for premium mobility, where the Company is positioned with Urbania
- EV penetration in medium-to-heavy passenger carriers is still early at 2-3%, leaving substantial headroom supported by government-led EV initiatives
- Healthy demand during the year across Tour and Travel, School Buses and buses for commuting professionals
- Broad-based platform performance: Traveller holding over 70% share of the core van segment, Urbania over 100% volume growth, Trax over 70% growth
- Electrification is expected to advance at different speeds across segments — electric mobility is most relevant for defined routes, higher daily mileage and last-mile applications, while conventional and alternative-fuel drivelines remain relevant elsewhere
- India's deeper trade engagement with major economies including the European Union creates a more favourable environment for Indian manufacturers with established global partnerships to expand internationally
- Watch item: geopolitical developments, energy and input availability, rising commodity prices and shipping/supply-chain disruption can impact both production and costs

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen the core vehicle businesses and reinforce leadership positions in chosen segments, pursuing growth with financial and operational discipline
- Application-based, multi-driveline product development — continued work on efficient ICE and CNG drivelines alongside electric mobility solutions, rather than assuming one technology replaces all others
- Refresh and premiumise the product portfolio: new-generation Traveller N range and Urbania DX, with Urbania positioned for premium passenger mobility
- Build out EV engineering capability, including an electric version of the Traveller platform and dedicated EV engineering infrastructure, assembly stations and a testing lab
- Expand geographically and place greater emphasis on exports, progressively preparing India-developed products for more sophisticated overseas markets
- Grow the defence and specialised mobility franchise through the Special Vehicle Division, building on purpose-built vehicle engineering (Gurkha supply to the Indian Army)
- Sustain the component contract-manufacturing business with global OEMs (engines and axles for Mercedes-Benz India, engines and CRFM modules for BMW India)
- Keep R&D spend at a consistent percentage of revenue, anchored on the state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre in Pune driving new product development
- Increase the share of renewable energy in manufacturing as part of a responsible and sustainable manufacturing approach

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes expansion mainly in qualitative terms rather than as a capex programme. On the energy side, the Company commissioned a rooftop solar power plant at Pithampur during the year, increasing the share of green energy in its energy mix, and continues to target 50% green energy by 2027 with a longer-term Net Zero emissions goal by 2050. Product-side expansion came through the introduction of the new-generation Traveller N range and Urbania DX, and through the Special Vehicle Division supplying the first lot of Gurkha vehicles to the Indian Army, with management pointing to continued opportunities in defence and specialised mobility. Development capability is centred on the Company's state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre in Pune, which drives new product development, engineering and technology solutions. Inorganically, after the close of the financial year the Company acquired 100% of Veera Tanneries Private Limited (VTPL) for `16,196 lacs, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary, and approved a loan of up to `2,000 lacs to vendor PKN Motors Private Limited. Management also frames geographic expansion — pursuing a wider range of geographical markets and greater emphasis on exports — as the next leg of growth, supported by continued investment in technology, people, processes and market development. No plant-wise capacity addition, commissioning timeline or rupee capex quantum is stated in the routed sections; the two named capex disclosures supplied (capital commitments and segment capital expenditure) arrive as labels only, with no figures attached.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Traveller maintained clear leadership in the core van segment, commanding over 70% market share
- Decade-plus contract manufacturing relationships with global OEMs: the 100,000th engine for BMW India was built during the year, and the 200,000th engine for Mercedes-Benz India followed, a relationship spanning over 50 years
- Debt-free position during the year, with the Board's Report noting zero debt service obligation and interest coverage improving sharply
- Joint venture with Rolls Royce Solutions GmbH (Force MTU Power Systems Private Limited, 51% held) gives access to global powertrain technology
- Engineering capability in purpose-built and defence vehicles, evidenced by the first lot of Gurkha vehicles supplied to the Indian Army
- Application-based, multi-driveline approach (efficient ICE, CNG and electric solutions) rather than a single-technology bet
- Broad-based platform growth in FY26: Urbania recorded over 100% volume growth and Trax over 70% growth, reducing dependence on a single platform

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Powertrain technology transition risk — no single winning technology — The MD&A states the industry is passing through a period of significant technological change with emphasis on electrification, alternative fuels and cleaner technologies, but that the transition will take place at different speeds across segments. The Company must fund parallel development of efficient ICE, CNG and electric drivelines without knowing which application shifts when; management explicitly says it will not assume one technology replaces all others.
- Geopolitical, energy and supply-chain disruption feeding into input costs — Management flags that recent geopolitical developments show how quickly events beyond India's borders can affect domestic industry, and that disruptions in energy and other essential inputs, rising commodity prices and disturbances to shipping and supply chains can impact both production and costs.
- Product quality, vehicle safety and customer-service failure (recall risk) — The BRSR materiality table identifies Customer Centricity as a risk: failure to meet changing customer expectations risks loss of loyalty and market share, while poor service can trigger legal action and negative publicity, and unattended vehicle safety issues can lead to accidents, injuries, fatalities and costly recalls.

The stability the Board's Report attributes to this business is therefore dependent on a very small number of contractual relationships and their model cycles.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
